name: Lamb koftas with tzatziki and salad
summary: Spiced lamb and mint koftas off the grill with cool garlic tzatziki and a chopped salad of tomato, cucumber, red onion and parsley.
about: Kofta, spiced minced meat shaped into balls or fingers, is cooked from Turkey and the Middle East to Iran and India; tzatziki is the Greek sauce of yoghurt, cucumber and garlic. On skewers, they cook as well on a braai as under the oven grill.

ingredients.name: English cucumber
ingredients.note: half grated for the tzatziki, half diced for the salad

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.note: juiced; 1 tbsp for the tzatziki, the rest for the salad

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.note: 2 tbsp for the salad, 1 tbsp for brushing the koftas

steps: If you are using wooden skewers, soak 8 of them in water for 30 minutes so they do not burn.
Grate half the cucumber onto a clean tea towel, gather it up and squeeze out as much water as you can.
Stir the squeezed cucumber into the yoghurt with the garlic, mint, 1 tbsp of the lemon juice and the salt. Cover and chill.
Toss the diced cucumber, tomatoes, red onion and parsley with the rest of the lemon juice, 2 tbsp of the oil and a pinch of salt.

Grate the onion, squeeze out its juice and put the pulp in a bowl with the lamb, garlic, spices, mint, parsley, salt and pepper. Mix with your hands for 1 minute, until evenly combined and slightly sticky.

With wet hands, divide the mixture into 8 and press each piece around a skewer into a sausage about 12 cm long. Chill for at least 15 minutes while the braai coals burn down to a steady heat, or while a griddle pan or the oven grill heats up.

Brush the koftas with the last 1 tbsp of oil. Cook over hot coals or on a griddle pan over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, until browned all over and firm, with no pink in the middle. Under the oven grill, cook them 10 cm from the element for 10 to 12 minutes, turning halfway.
Serve two koftas each with the salad and a generous spoonful of tzatziki.
prepNote: Shape the koftas and make the tzatziki up to a day ahead; keep both covered in the fridge.
